lina (People Ops): Quick Q — we have an employee (Ena) switching to a partial-pay schedule starting 6/15: ~60% FTE for 12 weeks. How do 401(k) deferrals behave? Are they auto-prorated by payroll or do we need to pause them and restart later? Also need clarity on company match during the reduced-pay window. cc @mike.payroll @olivia-benefits

mike.payroll: We don't automatically change deferral pct based on FTE. If the employee keeps the same percent, the $ withheld will be 60% of a full paycheck because gross pay is lower. Employer match is based on actual deferrals in the pay period (per plan doc). So match will be smaller if they defer the same percent and earn less.

olivia-benefits: Correct — under our plan (Fidelity admin), match is calculated on eligible compensation each pay. If Ena wants the same absolute $ contribution as before, they'd need to increase their deferral % manually. Otherwise it scales down with pay.

samir-engineering: Is there any minimum payroll withholding that might block contributions when pay is small? We have a contractor who went to partial pay and their 401k didn't deduct because net < taxes or processing fees.

mike.payroll: Good point. Payroll enforces the tax/benefit sequencing. If gross < tax/other required withholdings, the system can zero out voluntary deferrals for that period. For partial-pay at 60% we typically see deferrals still go through, but if someone drops to single-digit gross then it can trigger a skip. We can run a pre-check for Ena's projected pay runs to be safe.

olivia-benefits: Also: catch-up contributions (age 50+) are handled as additional % on top of regular deferral — if Ena is eligible and keeps the same % the catch-up portion will follow the same proration by pay amount. If she wants to preserve annual-dollar totals, she should submit a temporary deferral increase in the benefits portal.

lina (People Ops): Thanks. Timeline: Ena starts 6/15. Can payroll do a pre-check this week and let me know if any paychecks will result in zeroed deferrals? Manager needs to know whether to advise Ena to bump %.

mike.payroll: Yep — I can run a mock payroll for the next 3 cycles. Need Ena's anticipated gross for those checks. If you drop it here or DM I’ll run it. ETA EOD tomorrow. :white_check_mark:

hr-bot: Automatic reminder — benefits portal: https://benefits.redwood.example/deferrals. For any temporary deferral changes use the "Temporary change" flow and set an end date.

samir-engineering: One more: what about 401k loan repayments? If Ena currently has payroll-deducted loan repayments, do those continue on partial pay?

mike.payroll: Loan repayments are separate mandatory payroll deductions. They remain unless she requests a suspension and the plan admin approves. If gross pay becomes too small, loan deduction may be reduced or suspended per plan rules — we coordinate with Fidelity for that. I'll flag the client service rep if needed.

olivia-benefits: Action items: 1) Lina to confirm Ena's projected gross per pay cycle. 2) Mike to run mock payroll and confirm whether deferrals/loan repays will process. 3) Ena/manager to decide if they want to temporarily increase deferral % to hit dollar targets. We can support temporary change via portal.

lina (People Ops): Got it, I'll DM the numbers and loop Ena. Thanks everyone! :pray:
